terms.gloss: appear, come into sight; be seen
evidence: Sen. Ep. 77.1: subitō nōbīs hodiē Alexandrīnae nāvēs appāruērunt
Ter. Eun. 660: Ille autem bonus vir nusquam appāret.
terms.comment: Impersonal appāret with an accusative and infinitive is “it is clear that”, of what is plain to see; “it seems” is vidētur (Lewis & Short).
Of something coming out or arising where it was not before.

phrases.latin: subitō nōbīs hodiē Alexandrīnae nāvēs appāruērunt
phrases.english: suddenly today the ships from Alexandria came into sight

phrases.latin: Ille autem bonus vir nusquam appāret.
phrases.english: And that fine gentleman is nowhere to be seen.

phrases.latin: nec jam amplius ūllae appārent terrae, caelum undique et undique pontus
phrases.english: and no land is in sight any more, sky all round and sea all round

sources: Lewis & Short: appareo · Lewis & Short: exsisto
